decisions.reason: The gas tariff comparison sits close to the core data business, has its own web page, and costs little to maintain from the existing databases, so there is no shortfall that would trigger search for other uses of its resources.
The regional electricity tariff calculator is core-adjacent and visibly presented, and it fits the central platform strategy, so it meets aspirations and carrying it requires little slack.

The energy tariff calculator line overlaps with C and has only low web visibility, so consolidation is possible, but its several models reuse maintained data at low cost and slack in a growing industry favours keeping it for now.
The site-specific tariff comparison line builds directly on the firm's market data and is cheap to sustain, so despite modest visibility the firm can carry it while its results remain uncertain.
